{{nihongo |'''Shimon Sakaguchi''' | 坂口 志文 | Sakaguchi Shimon|born 19 January 1951}} is a Japanese [[immunologist]]. He is a [[Distinguished Professor|distinguished professor]] at [[Osaka University]] and a professor emeritus at [[Kyoto University]].<ref name="IFReC {{pipe}} Osaka University Immunology Frontier Research Center">{{cite web | title=Experimental Immunology – Osaka University Immunology Frontier Research Center | website=IFReC {{pipe}} Osaka University Immunology Frontier Research Center | url=http://www.ifrec.osaka-u.ac.jp/en/laboratory/shimon_sakaguchi/ | access-date=1 May 2021}}</ref>

His work includes the discovery of [[regulatory T cells]] and describing their role in the [[immune system]]. In 2025, he was jointly awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] with [[Mary E. Brunkow]] and [[Fred Ramsdell]].<ref name="Nobel">{{cite web
|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2025/summary/
|title=Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025
|website=NobelPrize.org
|access-date=6 October 2025
}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Shimon Sakaguchi was born on 19 January 1951 in [[Nagahama, Shiga]].<ref>[https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2025/sakaguchi/facts/ Shimon Sakaguchi  facts] nobelprize.org</ref> He received a medical degree in 1976 from the [[Graduate School of Medicine and Faculty of Medicine, Kyoto University|Faculty of Medicine]] at [[Kyoto University]]. In 1982, he also received a PhD degree from Kyoto University.<ref>{{cite EBO |title=Shimon Sakaguchi |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Fred-Ramsdell |access-date=8 October 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Sakaguchi undertook postdoctoral research in the United States at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Stanford University]] from 1983 to 1987 as a Lucille P. Markey Scholar.<ref name="jhuhub">{{cite web|url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2025/10/06/nobel-prize-shimon-sakaguchi-johns-hopkins-postdoctoral-studies/|title=Nobel laureate Shimon Sakaguchi conducted postdoctoral studies at Johns Hopkins in 1980s|work=The Hub |publisher=[[Johns Hopkins University]] |date=6 October 2025 |access-date=8 October 2025}}</ref> Later, he worked as an assistant professor in the Department of Immunology at the [[Scripps Research|Scripps Research Institute]].<ref name="jhuhub" />

After returning to Japan in 1991,<ref name="jhuhub" /> he worked at [[Riken]] as an investigator of the [[Japan Science and Technology Agency]].<ref name="gairdnerprofile">{{cite news |title=Shimon Sakaguchi |url=https://www.gairdner.org/winner/shimon-sakaguchi |access-date=8 October 2025 |work=[[Canada Gairdner International Award]] |publisher=[[Gairdner Foundation]]}}</ref> Later, he became the head of the Department of Immunopathology at the Tokyo Metropolitan Institute of Gerontology.<ref name=":1" /> Between 1998 and 2011, he worked as a professor and chairman of the Department of Experimental Pathology at the Institute for Frontier Medical Sciences of [[Kyoto University]]. From 2007 to 2011, he also served as the institute's director.<ref name="osakanobelbio">{{cite news |title=SAKAGUCHI Shimon Nobel Prize Laureate (Physiology or Medicine) |url=https://www.osaka-u.ac.jp/en/research/nobelprize/sakaguchi/top |access-date=8 October 2025 |publisher=[[Osaka University]]}}</ref> His lab was moved to [[University of Osaka|Osaka University]] in 2011.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Shimon Sakaguchi – ISNI Congress |url=https://www.isniweb.org/congress/profile/shimon-sakaguchi/ |access-date=6 October 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Research==
[[File:25-10-06-Nobel-Prize-FOXP3-Hegasy-v02.jpg|thumb|Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025: Pivotal role of FoxP3<sup>+</sup> T<sub>reg</sub> cells in peripheral immune tolerance]]
In a 1995 study, Sakaguchi and his colleagues showed the existence of [[regulatory T cell]]s, a previously unknown subset of [[T cell]]s expressing [[CD4]] and [[CD25]] that modulate the [[immune system]] and help maintain [[immune tolerance]].<ref name="naturenobel">{{cite news |last1=Naddaf |first1=Miryam |last2=Gibney |first2=Elizabeth |title=Medicine Nobel goes to scientists who revealed secrets of immune system 'regulation' |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-025-03193-3 |access-date=8 October 2025 |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |date=6 October 2025 |doi=10.1038/d41586-025-03193-3}}</ref> They injected [[BALB/c]] athymic mice with a suspension of [[CD4+ cell|CD4<sup>+</sup> cells]] previously depleted of CD25<sup>+</sup> cells and found that the mice subsequently developed [[autoimmune disease]]s (e.g. [[thyroiditis]] and [[gastritis]]). However, reconstitution of CD4<sup>+</sup>CD25<sup>+</sup> cells shortly after the initial injection of CD4<sup>+</sup>CD25<sup>−</sup> cells prevented the development of autoimmunity.<ref name="nobelbackground">{{cite web |last1=Karlsson Hedestam |first1=Gunilla |last2=Kämpe |first2=Olle |title=Scientific background 2025: Immune tolerance: The identification of regulatory T cells and FOXP3 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/10/advanced-medicineprize2025.pdf |website=nobelprize.org |publisher=[[Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute]] |access-date=8 October 2025 |date=6 October 2025}}</ref> In 2003, Sakaguchi's group demonstrated the importance of [[FOXP3]] in the development and function of regulatory T cells.<ref name="naturenobel" /><ref name="nobelbackground" />

==Honours and awards==
[[File:Shimon_Sakaguchi_20251006.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sakaguchi attended a press conference at the [[University of Osaka]] after the Nobel Prize laureates were announced on October 2, 2025]]
[[File:Shimon Sakaguchi 20151029.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Sakaguchi addressed at [[Canada Gairdner International Award]] Ceremony at the [[Royal Ontario Museum]] on 29 October 2015]]

On 6 October 2025, Sakaguchi was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] with [[Mary E. Brunkow]] and [[Fred Ramsdell]] "for their discoveries concerning [[peripheral tolerance|peripheral immune tolerance]]."<ref name="Nobel"/>

* 2004: [[William B. Coley Award]] (with [[Ethan M. Shevach]])<ref>[http://www.cancerresearch.org/about/annual-awards/william-b-coley William B. Coley Award-Award], ''Cancer Research Institute'' (cancerresearch.org)</ref>
* 2008: [[Keio Medical Science Prize]] (with [[Fred Gage]])<ref>[http://www.ms-fund.keio.ac.jp/prize/winner/prize2008.html The 2008 Keio Medical Science Prize Awardees] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180804050325/http://www.ms-fund.keio.ac.jp/prize/winner/prize2008.html |date=4 August 2018 }}, [[Keiō University]]</ref>
* 2009: [[Medals of Honor (Japan)|Medal of Honor]] with [[Medals of Honor (Japan)#Purple ribbon|Purple Ribbon]] (Japan)<ref>{{cite web |title=Distinguished Professor Shimon SAKAGUCHI of IFReC awarded Canada Gairdner International Award |date=26 March 2015 |publisher=Osaka University |url=http://www.osaka-u.ac.jp/en/news/topics/2015/03/20150326_01}}</ref>
* 2011: [[Asahi Prize]]<ref>[http://www.asahi.com/shimbun/award/asahi/english.html#2011 The Asahi Prize] ''[[Asahi Shimbun]]''</ref>
* 2012: Foreign associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences (United States)|National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/shimon-sakaguchi-rje99v/ Shimon Sakaguchi] National Academy of Sciences</ref>
* 2015: [[Chunichi Shimbun|Chunichi Culture]] Award<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shimon Sakaguchi awarded the Chunichi award {{!}} News & Topics {{!}} Osaka University Immunology Frontier Research Center |url=https://www.ifrec.osaka-u.ac.jp/en/topics/20150525-0423.htm |access-date=6 October 2025 |website=www.ifrec.osaka-u.ac.jp}}</ref>
* 2015: [[Canada Gairdner International Award]]<ref name="gairdnerprofile" />
* 2016, 2018, 2021: [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= [[Asian Scientist]] |access-date= 13 March 2025 |quote= |language= }}</ref>

* 2017: [[Person of Cultural Merit]] (Japan)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shimon Sakaguchi was named a Person of Cultural Merit of Japan {{!}} News & Topics {{!}} Osaka University Immunology Frontier Research Center |url=https://www.ifrec.osaka-u.ac.jp/en/topics/20171025-0919.htm |access-date=6 October 2025 |website=www.ifrec.osaka-u.ac.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 November 2017 |title=Cultural Merit awards conferred upon Shimon Sakaguchi, Shuh Narumiya, and Michio Muramatsu (24 October 2017) |url=https://www.kyoto-u.ac.jp/en/news/2017-11-21-2 |access-date=6 October 2025 |website=KYOTO UNIVERSITY |language=en}}</ref>
